title: Quasi-compact affine-test atlas predicate for presheaf morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with test schemes and universes as in [def-weil-size-convention] and [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $G,F$ be presheaves of sets on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)$ and $g:G\to F$ a natural transformation. The quasi-compact affine-test atlas predicate for $g$ means that for every affine scheme $Z$ over $S$ and map $h:h_Z\to F$, there exist a scheme $U$ over $S$, a morphism $p:U\to Z$, and a natural transformation $q:h_U\to G$ with $g\circ q=h\circ h_p$, such that $U$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and the induced map $(q,h_p):h_U\to G\times_F h_Z$ is etale and surjective in the scheme-test sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Here $h_Z$ and $h_U$ are the represented presheaves. On algebraic spaces this is the affine-test formulation of quasi-compactness.
